findings.message: T001 is not fully executable: it does not enumerate the seven target briefing file paths or symbols; an executor must invent the file boundary.
T003 is not fully executable: it names a maintainer-checklist check but omits the target checklist file/path or symbol.

T001 restates upstream behavior/design rationale in prose ('make role-statement violations reportable, retain the existing categories as priority categories, and preserve What NOT to report') instead of using only target + operation + anchor cite.

T002 restates upstream behavior/design rationale in prose ('retain plan-artifacts.md and all document-inspection noise controls in their closed form') instead of using only target + operation + anchor cite.
The S1 section description repeats the upstream contract ('without weakening their existing non-reportable boundaries') rather than stating only the implementation target, operation, and anchors.

The S2 section description repeats the upstream closure/boundary behavior ('preserve the closed plan-artifacts document-inspection briefing') rather than stating only the implementation target, operation, and anchors.

The S3 section description repeats the upstream behavioral contract ('guard against a role-statement prohibition that lacks applicable reportability guidance') rather than stating only the implementation target, operation, and anchors.

The `plan.summary` GO-01 entry restates upstream behavior/design rationale ('while preserving the closed document-inspection boundary and noise controls') instead of limiting the plan section to executable traceability.
The `plan.summary` GO-02 entry restates the upstream behavioral contract ('detects role-statement/category contradictions') instead of limiting the plan section to executable traceability.

IN-03 requires preserving `What NOT to report` in every reviewer briefing, but its coverage lists only T001, which targets the seven code-layer prompts. T002 owns the remaining ADR/spec/types/impl-plan prompts and already carries AC-02/OUT-02, so add T002 to IN-03 and its task/section anchor lists.

T002 (repeated by S2) says to update `.harness/custom/review-prompts/plan-artifacts.md`, but that file was deleted and neither exists in the current tree nor is created by another task. The executor must invent whether to resurrect or omit it; remove the dead target or explicitly define a creation operation supported by the upstream scope.

この系譜は 7 本の briefing 新設と `plan-artifacts.md` 形式の踏襲を ADR 2026-06-18-1406 D6 に帰属させていますが、D6 が決めているのは `.harness/custom/**` の利用者所有・never-clobber 境界です。対象範囲と形式を決めたのはそれぞれ D3 と D4 であり、現状の引用は新 ADR の根拠系譜を誤って示します。D3–D4 を引用してください。
AC-03 の「文書検査系の既存のノイズ抑制動作を変えない」は、spec 内で確認手順や判定可能な条件が定義されておらず、文書内容の目視だけでは決定的に検証できないため、受入条件として非観測可能です。

CN-02 leaves “whether the defect classes are closed under enumeration” undefined, while IN-05/AC-04 neither prescribe the result for each SoT briefing nor provide an objective classification procedure. Downstream work must therefore invent whether ADR/spec/types/impl-plan should be closed or semi-open, and AC-04 cannot deterministically pass or fail.

The related-convention citations to `coding-principles.md` / “No Panics in Library Code” and `prefer-type-safe-abstractions.md` / “Rule” govern Rust production code and type design, not this docs-only change to reviewer-briefing category semantics. They are narratively off-topic grounding for the spec.
